title: Safety at work: why accidents are not “accidents”
author: Editorial Desk
summary: Most workplace deaths can be prevented with simple rules, training and inspection.
body:
The ILO estimates that millions of workers die every year from work-related accidents and diseases. India has seen deaths in mines, construction sites, chemical factories and sewers.

## Common causes

- **Lack of training** and protective equipment.
- **Poor maintenance** of machinery.
- **Overcrowding** and weak fire safety.
- **Hazardous cleaning work**, such as manual cleaning of sewers, which is prohibited by law.
- **Pressure** to meet targets.

## The legal base

The OSH Code lays down duties of employers, rights of workers, requirements for safety committees and standards for specific industries. The Directorate General of Factory Advice Service and Labour Institutes (DGFASLI) and the Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS) support enforcement.

## What workers can do

- Insist on **protective equipment** and training.
- Report **hazards** through the safety committee or the union.
- Seek **compensation** after any accident, under the Employees' Compensation Act or ESI.

## BMS's view

Safety is not a cost. It is part of production. Investigating each accident and fixing responsibility is the first step in preventing the next.
